acceptance: In a disposable repository, batch-member-create starts the member at the integration head commit and records role, ids and base.

batch-member-check refuses an unsynced member, a non-Python change without named tests and a dirty tree; on success it records a result keyed by member head and integration head, with exempt-only recorded as not reviewed.
pr-open and pr-fanout in a member worktree refuse with no push and no hosted mutation; ordinary worktrees are unaffected.

In a disposable repository, batch-start creates a role=integration worktree and prints a register_batch payload that a scratch todo-db server accepts; batch-member-create names the branch feat/<batch>--<member>; merged to develop.
context: Decision gate: start only after benchbox-todo-db-batch-v2-runtime-20261101, worktree-create-base-ref-20261101 and local-oracle-member-review-20261101 are done. Owner decision 2026-11-01 (owner answer in the choice dialog, BenchBox session 01a19729, 2026-11-01): "Same bar as a standalone PR" [option text: an exempt-only member is recorded as not reviewed, distinct from a pass; the final PR's hosted oracle-gate reviews the combined change]. The role marker is git config, not lifecycle metadata: write preflight skips the ownership claim without a session id (worktree_lifecycle_metadata.py:228-229) and only Make targets read the role. worktree_lifecycle.sh:164-171 strips inherited benchbox.* keys, so set the marker after creation. Members never write into the leader's worktree. Guardrails: deliver as an ordinary serial PR to develop (AGENTS.md: feature delivery cannot deliver the changes that make it possible); write only from a linked worktree made with make worktree-create and checked with make agent-write-preflight, never the primary clone; stage explicit paths, never git add -A; no explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001, make comment-policy-check); heavy test runs only through lock-taking entry points, never BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK; never weaken hold labels, the unresolved-thread refusal, oracle-gate, duration or suite gates; add a changelog.d fragment (CHANGELOG_INTERNAL when nothing is user-visible); durable artifacts carry no session or phase labels; cited line numbers are leads, so re-read the code before editing; tests prove behaviour, never wiring or wording.
description: Add make/batch.mk, included from Makefile, with the leader's batch-start and the member-side targets; logic lives in scripts/batch_integration.py subcommands. batch-start creates the integration worktree with worktree-create, marks it with git config --worktree benchbox.batch.role=integration, and prints the register_batch payload with the scope hash from pr_landing's scope-hash code. batch-member-create makes a feat/<batch>--<member> worktree with BASE set to the current integration head commit (Git refuses feat/<batch>/<member> beside feat/<batch>), marks role=member and records batch id, member id and source base. batch-member-check refuses unless the member is clean and contains the current integration head (the member merges it in and resolves conflicts first); then runs pr-preflight BASE=<integration head>, refuses non-Python changes unless the member names their tests, runs the changelog check and the member-mode local review, and records the result in the member worktree config keyed by member head and integration head. pr-open and pr-fanout refuse in a role=member worktree before any push.
